title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault‑Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired design using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one source generation invalid and excluded per the preregistered rule). Baseline (blind repair) satisfied the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) satisfied it in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired counts: n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini and recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120). The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis executor; the frozen harmful-change mapping and the per-episode traces required to compute that preregistered statistic are archived and we describe the exact artifact locations and compact operational mapping needed for independent reconstruction in Methods. We therefore do not present a preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair verdict in this paper but provide full reproducibility paths.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed as aides in network operations (NetOps) for tasks such as intent-to-configuration translation and automated remediation. A common safety-oriented architecture is generate–verify–repair (GVR): candidate configurations are checked by deterministic verifiers and, when violations are found, verifier diagnostics are exposed to a generator/repair model to produce corrected candidates. Prior controlled and empirical work in code and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) settings reports that inserting deterministic verifiers between generation and acceptance can increase verifier-detected pass rates while exposing new failure modes (e.g., verifier-exploitation) and imposing interaction costs [1], [2], [3], [4]. Survey and field studies of LLMs in NetOps/AIOps emphasize that read-oriented usefulness does not automatically imply safe closed-loop changes without strong verification and conservative orchestration [5].

Motivation and research question. Controlled paired evidence on verifier-guided repair applied to vendor CLIs with preregistered realistic fault operators is sparse. A practical methodological pitfall is intervention informativeness: diagnostics can only affect outcomes when initial candidates trigger actionable violations. To ensure informativeness we ran a preregistered deterministic controlled-fault injection and a paired design that shares the same controlled-fault candidate across arms. Our research question: Does exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow reduce residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults?
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair pipelines have been empirically studied across adjacent domains. Work formalizing GVR architectures for regulated code generation demonstrates that interposing deterministic verification oracles and iterating with typed diagnostics can convert stochastic generation into a convergent correction process for mechanically-checkable defect classes [1]. Recent verifier-first IaC evaluations report large verifier-detected pass‑rate gains from verifier‑guided refinement and identify design elements (retrieval, prompt optimization, retry budget) that materially affect outcomes [2]. Controlled analyses of iterative-refinement pipelines document verifier-exploitation pathologies—single-proxy auditors can be optimized in ways that degrade the true target property—even in weight-frozen, prompt-only revision loops [3]. Empirical studies of verifier-mediated agents also report a measurable "verifier tax": interposition increases interaction horizons and compute while not guaranteeing safe goal attainment in some multi-step settings [4]. Finally, surveys and field case studies for agentic NetOps/AIOps synthesize an evidence–assurance gap: results are strongest for read-oriented assistance but weaken for closed-loop configuration changes, motivating controlled, verifier-grounded experiments with explicit safety instrumentation [5]. Each numbered citation above maps to the corresponding verified bibliographic record in References and supports the immediately adjacent claim.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study was preregistered under the archived plan vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration document archived in the execution manifest). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline, where binary success requires both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement.

Design and adapter semantics. Confirmatory execution used the adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 under its shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each preregistered task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was produced and reused unchanged across both conditions. Each pair received exactly one initial generation (shared) and one repair opportunity per condition; baseline denotes blind repair (no verifier diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. The declared model for confirmatory execution is gpt-5-mini; the archived model configuration records temperature = null (unset). Null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Per-call runtime sampling parameters and metadata for each hosted-model invocation are archived and available to auditors at execution/execution_log.jsonl (per-call records) and execution/model_configuration.json (declared settings) in the evidence bundle; these artifacts contain the recorded provider-call events and sampling metadata for every model call executed in the confirmatory run.

Controlled-challenge sampling and missingness. To ensure intervention activation we preregistered deterministic controlled faults (task indices 1..40) that inject actionable violations (e.g., missing required restore, protected-interface changes). Confirmatory task_count was fixed at 40. The execution manifest records source_generation_attempt_count = 40 with source_valid_count = 39 (one invalid source generation produced an unscorable pair and was excluded under the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule). Exclusions and all terminal error reasons are archived in execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl; the analysis missingness file is archived at analysis/missingness_summary.csv.

Scoring rules and the harmful-change mapping. The primary success predicate required both the deterministic vendor‑CLI validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) and simulator agreement. The preregistration froze a harmful-change labeling schema used for the preregistered harmful-overrepair hypothesis: an episode is labeled harmful if the post-repair validator trace contains any violation code in {PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE, UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE}. The transformation artifact that implements this mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json. The confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; Section Results explains the status and provides exact artifact locations and the compact operational mapping needed to reproduce that preregistered statistic deterministically from archived per-episode traces.

Statistical analysis. The preregistered primary test is an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent exact paired binomial) with discordant-pair counts, absolute paired risk difference, two-sided exact p-value, and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Multiplicity: a single predefined primary test; subgroup analyses are exploratory. Missingness sensitivity analyses were preregistered (primary excludes incomplete pairs; sensitivity treats missing episodes as failures). All per-episode artifacts and provider traces required to reproduce the analysis are archived (execution/raw_results.jsonl; execution/scoring/*.json; analysis/*.csv).
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary confirmatory outcomes. Planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs) with failed_episode_count = 2. Hosted-model calls used = 118 (<= planned maximum 120). Source-generation attempts = 40 with source_valid_count = 39 and source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1; the single invalid source-generation caused one excluded pair under the preregistered rule. Run timestamps and full execution manifest are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Primary confirmatory outcomes (complete_pairs = 39). Baseline (blind repair) success = 30/39 = 0.7692307692307693. Guarded (verifier-guided) success = 38/39 = 0.9743589743589743. Paired contingency counts (guarded, baseline): n11 = 29, n10 = 9 (guarded-only), n01 = 1 (baseline-only), n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The archived analysis artifacts analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv and analysis/condition_summary.csv contain the supporting CSVs and are recorded in the evidence manifest.

Preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation: status and reproducibility path. The preregistration included a confirmatory safety hypothesis limiting absolute harmful-overrepair increase to <= 5 percentage points. The archived confirmatory analysis executor produced the primary paired binary result but did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation (secondary_results = []). Because that preregistered aggregation was not produced in the archived confirmatory summary, we do not present a retroactive preregistered confirmatory safety claim here. To enable exact independent reproduction of the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation from the archived artifacts, auditors should: (1) iterate the complete pairs listed in analysis/missingness_summary.csv; (2) for each condition read validation_after.violation_codes from execution/scoring/<episode>.json (or execution/raw_results.jsonl); (3) apply the compact mapping (label harmful if validation_after.violation_codes contains PROTECTED_INTERFACE_CHANGE or UNINTENDED_STATE_CHANGE); and (4) compute paired harmful counts and the paired difference per the analysis plan. The transformation implementing this mapping is archived at execution/transformation_manifest.json. Because the confirmatory executor did not run this aggregation, any harmful-overrepair aggregation computed outside the archived analysis must be treated as an independent reconstruction and labeled exploratory unless recomputed and archived following the preregistered pipeline.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-pair JSON scoring artifacts are archived (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json, task-000002-*.json, task-000003-*.json, etc.). Example diagnostics illustrate mechanisms where guarded repairs removed protected-interface violations or restored required command sequences that blind repair sometimes omitted; these per-episode traces are present in execution/scoring/*.json.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and mechanism. The confirmatory paired result shows a substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated success when deterministic verifier diagnostics are exposed to the repair model under shared controlled-fault pairing semantics. The paired design isolates the effect of diagnostic exposure because both arms received the same initial controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets. Archived per-episode traces illustrate plausible causal pathways: diagnostics identify concrete violation classes that guide targeted edits in guarded repairs, reducing protected-interface changes and restoring required sequences.

Safety caveat and unresolved preregistered aggregation. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair statistic is unresolved in the confirmatory archive because that aggregation was not produced by the archived analysis executor. We supply the exact compact mapping and artifact locations needed for deterministic reproduction so auditors can compute the preregistered safety metric from archived per-episode traces; until that preregistered aggregation is recomputed and archived following the preregistered pipeline, no confirmatory safety verdict is reported here.

Operational implications and verifier tax. The experiment required additional model–verifier interactions: hosted-model calls used = 118 and stage counts record one source generation plus paired repair episodes per condition. These instrumented counts allow exploratory computation of model-call cost per avoided failure, though larger-scale operational cost/latency generalization is outside this confirmatory run. Practitioners should ensure verifier coverage for critical safety properties, audit harmful-change indicators (using frozen mappings like our preregistered rule), and budget for verifier-mediated call counts and latency prior to closed-loop deployment.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: model sampling nondeterminism (temperature recorded as null/unset) and exactly-one initial sampled generation per pair limit claims about deterministic generation effects; differences across arms stem from diagnostic exposure under the adapter contract. Construct validity: primary success depends on deterministic verifier and simulator agreement; both impose construct limitations. External validity: a single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic controlled-fault bank constrain generalization to diverse vendor equipment and live operator streams. Conclusion validity: complete_pairs = 39 yields reasonable precision for the observed primary contrast but limited power for fine-grained subgroup inference.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment using hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier+simulator-validated configuration success (≈ +20.51 percentage points; p = 0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769, 0.3590]). This result is bounded to the preregistered synthetic task bank, the declared model (gpt-5-mini), and the archived deterministic verifier and simulator. The preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation was not produced by the archived confirmatory analysis executor and therefore remains unresolved for the confirmatory claim; the frozen harmful-change mapping and per-episode traces required to compute it are archived and we document the exact reconstruction path in Methods. We release the full artifact bundle for reproducible reaggregation and recommend multi-model, multi-verifier replications and larger-scale cost/latency studies to assess operational feasibility and safety at NetOps scale.

disclosure_statement: Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model used for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version recorded in execution/model_configuration.json). Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1 (preregistration archived in the execution manifest). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10). Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed the literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation without manual human editing of technical manuscript content. Execution artifacts and per-episode provider-call records are archived (key artifact locations cited in Methods) and the execution followed the preregistered stopping rule; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects for the observed primary contrast but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires larger-scale study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (multi-verifier designs, calibrated abstention, uncertainty quantification).

Preregistered confirmatory harmful-overrepair aggregation not present in archived confirmatory summary: the archived confirmatory analysis executor did not compute the preregistered harmful-overrepair aggregation; the per-episode traces and transformation manifest required to compute it are archived and available for independent reaggregation, but the preregistered confirmatory safety verdict is therefore unresolved in this paper.
